parsed.basis: Faafu is a rural southern atoll made up of small inhabited islands with close-knit, socially conservative communities, where public life follows strict Islamic dress and gender-segregation norms and there is no isolated tourist-resort enclave to insulate visitors as elsewhere in the Maldives. Tourism is minimal, anonymity is low, and island councils and local police enforce public morality, while national law criminalises same-sex conduct, provides no protection against gender-identity discrimination, and offers no transgender-specific document, facility or care rules. A transgender visitor who was discovered would therefore be conspicuous to residents and officials, exposed to moral condemnation and possible police intervention under broadly framed offences, with little practical recourse, although documented enforcement against visitors and capital punishment are not part of the national record.
